pageCache.pageTitle: Tewkesbury Academy celebrates GCSEs   - Tewkesbury Academy
pageCache.text:
Tewkesbury Academy celebrates GCSEs
Students at Tewkesbury Academy are celebrating their GCSE results today (Thursday 20 August). The hall was brimming with families and staff congratulating Year 11 on their hard work and determination. The Academy was particularly pleased to see a number of students achieving high grades across the board as well as strong performances in subjects such as photography, history, French and music.
Ms McGillycuddy, Principal, said “We are incredibly proud of all our students particularly this year where they have shown extra determination and resilience. Tewkesbury is a wonderful place to grow up and Tewkesbury Academy is a great place to learn. We look forward to seeing many of our Year 11s again when they join our sixth form next month.
The Academy would also like to thank its staff, families and wider community for their continued support in helping students achieve their goals and realise their potential.
If any young people are interested in joining our ever-improving sixth form, please do get in touch for a conversation. Please contact sixthform@ta.clf.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Tewkesbury students get hands-on with nature - Tewkesbury Academy
pageCache.text:
Tewkesbury students get hands-on with nature
Team Science at Tewkesbury Academy recently took Key Stage 3 students on an exciting trip to Tewkesbury Nature Reserve, where they explored the local wildlife, woodlands and waterways.
The students enjoyed getting hands-on with nature, taking part in a range of outdoor activities, including bug hunting, fire lighting and river dipping.
The visit provided a valuable opportunity for students to explore their local environment, develop practical skills and learn beyond the classroom.
One Year 7 student said: “The nature reserve was very fun. I loved that we went river dipping and my group caught three fish. I can’t remember the fish names, but it was really fun! I also loved that we used cotton wool, newspaper and wood, with flint and steel in a biscuit tin, to build our own fire.
“At the end of the trip, I didn’t want to go home. It was my favourite day of Year 7.”
A spokesperson for Tewkesbury Academy said: “We are delighted that our students had such an enjoyable and memorable experience at Tewkesbury Nature Reserve.
“Opportunities like this bring learning to life, allowing students to develop practical skills, build confidence and deepen their appreciation of the natural world.
“We look forward to continuing our partnership with the reserve and organising more exciting outdoor learning experiences in the future.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Tewkesbury students enjoy an inspiring day in London - Tewkesbury Academy
pageCache.text:
Tewkesbury students enjoy an inspiring day in London
A group of 50 design and technology students from Tewkesbury Academy enjoyed an exciting and educational trip to London to explore the worlds of fashion, art and food.
The students split into groups to experience a range of cultural and creative attractions, linking their classroom learning with real-world inspiration.
One group visited the Fashion and Textile Museum, where they explored the work of Ossie Clark, the iconic British fashion designer renowned for helping define the style of London’s ‘Swinging Sixties’ and early 1970s. Viewing his designs gave students an insight into the creativity, craftsmanship and influence of British fashion.
The group then visited Tate, home to the national collection of British art and an extensive collection of international modern and contemporary art. The visit offered students the opportunity to experience a diverse range of artistic styles and ideas, providing further inspiration for their own creative work.
Meanwhile, students studying food technology took part in a Walk, Eat, London tour of Borough Market, one of the capital’s best-known historic food markets, located near London Bridge. Students explored the market’s vibrant food culture, discovered a variety of ingredients and flavours, and gained a greater appreciation of food, its origins and its place in contemporary society.
Tamsin Cummins, Head of Design & Technology, and Helen Butt, Design & Technology teacher, said:
“Trips like this are a fantastic opportunity for our students to take their learning beyond the classroom.
“From exploring iconic fashion designs and world-renowned art collections to discovering the rich variety of food at Borough Market, the day allowed students to gain fresh inspiration, broaden their knowledge and make meaningful connections with their studies.
“It was wonderful to see them engaging with new experiences and developing their understanding of the creative industries.”

Careers at Tewkesbury Academy
Across our wide and varied curriculum, we embed careers learning at every stage, with employers coming in to support our teaching teams, highlighting to young people the relevance of their school-based learning to future careers.
We value the importance of excellent impartial careers advice and work with a variety of external agencies, local post-16 providers and higher education establishments to share advice and guidance on a range of qualifications such as GCSEs, A-levels, BTEC Diplomas, HNCs, HNDs and degrees. The programme offers extensive advice and guidance on the future of each student. Knowing what to do next, whether it is university, sixth form, further education college or an apprenticeship, is central to our careers and work-related learning programme. All students are fully supported in receiving appropriate guidance to help them decide on their next steps, with plenty of opportunities to visit further and higher education establishments throughout their time at our school.
Here at Tewkesbury Academy we enjoy excellent relationships with a wide variety of employers from across the county. This enables us to ensure our students have multiple encounters with employers throughout their time with us, across a whole host of enrichment activities. These include an apprenticeship and careers fairs for Years 7-13 aimed at broadening horizons and introducing students to careers they have not encountered before; workplace visits to local employers; careers talks from business partners; work experience in Year 12; enterprise and employability skills-building days, mock interview practice and mentoring schemes.
We are continually looking for volunteers who are willing to share their own experiences of the working world and we are passionate that all students should be made aware of the vast array of opportunities and pathways available to them. We believe that with labour market information provided directly by our local business partners, students are able to make considered and informed choices about their futures.
If you feel you may be able to support our careers programme, please email our Careers Adviser at sarah.baird@clf.uk or phone 01684 292152.
We value the importance of future goals and raising aspirations and tailor our programme to make sure each student is equipped with the employability skills needed for the modern workplace and a clear idea of their next steps whenever they finish their studies with us at Tewkesbury Academy. Students across all key stages benefit from a careers programme delivered during their PSHEE lessons and we aim to ensure this fully covers all aspects of careers exploration and employability skills. Our careers lessons are designed to promote equality, diversity and social mobility, and challenge stereotypes. All students are given the opportunity to develop their knowledge of future pathways, set careers goals and fulfil their own potential.
Measuring impact of the careers programme
The careers lead evaluates the input of what goes into the provision, including policies, programmes and curriculum time. Output evaluations are also made which assess the impact of the learning on students. Output evaluations can be summarised in this model, taken from derby.ac.uk
Unifrog – The Complete Destinations Platform
To compliment our extensive careers programme, we subscribe Unifrog, an award-winning, online destinations platform designed to offer tailored support to students when choosing their next step after school. Students in all years have continual access to this website from year 7 to 13, throughout their school life.
Unifrog is designed to support learners in making informed decisions about their futures, with a range of tools that are suitable for all year groups. Each student has their own account that provides a range of information related to their interests and aspirations.
Key features of the platform for students include: • Psychometric testing quizzes • Career and subject exploration • Webinars and interactive short courses • Self-reflection and portfolio building tools • Search tools for live apprenticeship and employer opportunities, and university courses • Application and essay-building tools
All students have an account created using their school email address as their login which is made up as follows:
firstname.lastname@ta.clf.uk and we use Microsoft Outlook. Students access the platform by clicking a link in their welcome email, or by logging in with their school email address – https://www.unifrog.org/sign-in. If the students clicks “reset password” a link will go to their school email inbox and they can create a password from scratch if they have not already done so.
Parent / Carer Login We encourage parents and carers to use the platform with your child so you can support them through the process of deciding on their next steps. To do this, we’ve set up a parent login so that you can use Unifrog as if you were a student yourself, allowing you to access the same resources and tools as your child. To create a parent account, go to unifrog.org/code and input the sign-up code: SCDFfamily

pageCache.pageTitle: Students gain insight into technology careers - Tewkesbury Academy
pageCache.text:
Students gain insight into technology careers
A group of Year 8 students from Tewkesbury Academy recently attended the BT Work Ready at BT’s headquarters in Birmingham, where they gained valuable insight into the world of work and the exciting opportunities available within the technology and telecommunications industry.
The visit focused on the importance of digital skills in the modern workplace, highlighting how technology is transforming the way people communicate, collaborate and solve problems. Students learned that digital skills are now essential in almost every career sector, from business and healthcare to engineering, education and the creative industries.
During the event, BT colleagues introduced students to the wide range of careers available within BT Group, including roles in cyber security, software engineering, data analysis, project management, customer service, marketing, network engineering and business operations. Students discovered that there are many pathways into these careers, including apprenticeships, degree apprenticeships, college courses and university study.
One of the highlights of the day was the opportunity to work and learn on the 17th floor of BT’s impressive Birmingham office. From this vantage point, students enjoyed spectacular views across the city, as well as the opportunity to tour the building and experience a modern working environment. Three Snowhill provides workspace for up to 3,500 BT employees, making it BT’s largest hub outside London.
Students also took part in interactive activities designed to develop teamwork, communication, problem-solving and employability skills. The visit provided an inspiring glimpse into a professional working environment and helped students begin to understand how the subjects they study at school can connect to future careers in technology and digital industries.
Students left feeling motivated by the variety of opportunities available and with a greater understanding of the growing importance of digital skills in an increasingly connected world.
A spokesperson for the academy said: “The visit to BT gave our students a fantastic opportunity to see first-hand how the skills they are developing in school can connect to exciting careers in the real world.
“It was particularly valuable for students to meet professionals working across such a wide range of roles and to discover the many different routes into the technology industry.
“We hope the experience has inspired our students to think ambitiously about their futures and recognise the opportunities that are available to them.”

Gloucestershire County Council has launched a new school attendance strategy aimed at helping pupils and families overcome barriers to regular school attendance.
The strategy, launched to coincide with the start of the new school year, focuses on providing practical support to families rather than taking a purely punitive approach when children are repeatedly absent from school.
The council says the initiative is designed to help families address the reasons behind absence and make it easier for children to attend school regularly.
BBC Radio Gloucestershire spoke to Kathleen McGillycuddy, Principal of Tewkesbury Academy, to hear her reaction to the new approach and its potential impact on pupils, families and schools across the county.

pageCache.text:
Tewkesbury students explore the future of cyber and technology
Year 8 students from Tewkesbury Academy attended Empower, an annual hands-on cyber and technology event hosted at the University of Gloucestershire, where they had the opportunity to explore the exciting world of digital technology, cybersecurity and innovation.
Now in its fifth year, Empower is an engaging and interactive event designed to inspire young people, particularly those who may not yet have considered a career in the digital sector. The event encourages students to discover the wide range of opportunities available in digital technology (Digitech), cybersecurity and frontier technologies.
Throughout the day, students enthusiastically participated in a range of practical workshops and challenges designed to develop their problem-solving, teamwork and digital skills. Activities included cracking a code to unlock a chest, protecting a city from a cyberattack, completing a digital escape room and attempting to steal a secret chicken recipe from a chicken shop.
A particular highlight of the day was the digital escape room challenge, in which Ellen, a Year 8 student, achieved the highest score and finished top of the leaderboard at the end of the event. In recognition of her achievement, Ellen won a family cinema voucher.
Tom Lakin, Lead Teacher in Computing and IT at Tewkesbury Academy, said: “Students were a credit to the school, showing excellent enthusiasm, teamwork and problem-solving skills throughout the day.
“It was a fantastic opportunity for students to explore careers in cyber and computing while developing and applying real-world skills used by industry professionals every day.”

Extra-Curricular Activities
Students should discuss attending clubs with their subject teacher first to ensure they are aware of the day, when the club is starting, venue and club start and end time and then discuss attending with parents, in advance. Clear arrangements must be made regarding getting home safely/suitable collection point.
Music and singing lessons
We are pleased to offer a wide range of lessons on musical instruments, music technology and singing. These are delivered by our team of visiting music/vocal teachers and take place across the school day. This is in addition to the normal class music lessons in Key Stage 3 and for GCSE. Lessons can be started as a total beginner in September or at any point during your child’s time at school, as long as there is availability.
Students can opt for 20 or 30 minute lessons and there is the option to share a lesson in some instruments. Whilst students do come out of their subject lessons for this there is a rota system so that they avoid having lessons at the same time each week. There is the option to hire instruments if necessary from the County music hub. The peripatetic teacher will make the necessary arrangements with the school based on the information supplied by parents/carers. Tuition fee discounts are available, for example, if you are in receipt of Free School Meals.
Please click on this link if you wish to sign up for instrumental/vocal lessons at Tewkesbury Academy. For further information please email Rachael.patrick@clf.uk
The Duke of Edinburgh’s Award
Tewkesbury Academy has been running the Duke of Edinburgh’s Award successfully since 1986.
The Duke of Edinburgh’s Award is the world’s leading achievement award for young people. The award provides a balanced programme of activities that develops the whole person – mind, body and soul – in an environment of social interaction and teamworking.
Doing DofE is a brilliant way for young people to discover just how much they are capable of. It gives them the chance to make new friends, follow their passions, learn new skills, and make a difference within our community. Achieving a DofE Award is a great way to impress employers too. It helps young people to see themselves differently and gain a new level of confidence. The DofE is non-competitive and a powerful way for every young person to build belief in themselves, whatever their background, interests, and abilities.
How it works?
There are three levels of DofE Award – Bronze, Silver, and Gold. To achieve their Award, young people will need to complete four sections – Volunteering, Physical, Skills and the Expedition.
Young people can choose what they would like to do for the first three sections, and we will provide all the guidance and support they need. The Expedition involves spending two days and one night in the countryside in groups of 4 to 7. Staff will be on hand to support the young people whilst out on Expedition, and we provide comprehensive training beforehand to ensure everyone is fully prepared and has the best possible experience.
Next steps
Participants can be between the ages of 14 and 24 and we hope lots of our young people will take this opportunity to get involved with DofE. The scheme is launched in Year 9.
If your child is interested in taking part but the cost might be a barrier, then please do get in touch. If you have any other questions, please feel free to contact Tewkesbury Academy’s Award leader Mr Andrew Phillips via DofE@ta.clf.uk. The DofE website dofe.org – has a lot of useful information too.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Premium & Catch-up Funding - Tewkesbury Academy
pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium & Catch-up Funding
‘Disadvantaged pupils’ are those who have claimed free school meals at any point in the past six years and pupils in care, or who left care through adoption or another formal route. Evidence shows that the progress and achievement of disadvantaged pupils is normally lower than that of ‘other’ pupils. Additionally, schools are allocated Service Premium, to support the pastoral care of pupils who have a parent serving in the armed forces or a parent who is retired with a pension from the Ministry of Defence.
Evidence from research suggests Pupil Premium spending is most effective when schools use a tiered approach, targeting spending across the following 3 areas:
Teaching – schools arrange training and professional development for all their staff to improve the impact of teaching and learning for pupils.
Academic and pastoral support – schools should decide on the main issues stopping their pupils from succeeding at school and use the pupil premium to support extra help.
Wider approaches – this may include broader use of the Pupil Premium
​The grant does not have to be completely spent by schools in the fiscal year; some or all of it may be carried forward to future financial years.

The evening will start at 5:30pm in the Gym with a presentation from the Principal, Ms McGillycuddy. This will give you the opportunity to hear more about our vision, values and life at Tewkesbury Academy. Should the Gym reach its capacity for the presentation, we will re-run the talk starting at 6.15pm
Tours of the school will follow on from the presentation where you will get to see our excellent facilities, sample lessons and speak with subject staff. During tours, the Canteen will be open serving complimentary refreshments and taster meals.
The evening ends at 7:30pm.
Parking is available in the large car park nearest to the motorway, with additional parking at Alderman Knight School.
To help our planning, we ask families to book a place using the link below (see under downloads).
Spaces on our open morning tours are limited and our remaining open mornings (due to take place on 29 September and 15 October) are now FULLY booked. Please contact lyndsey.woodward@clf.uk to enquire about a school visit.
We look forward to welcoming you.

The Cabot Learning Federation
A mature Multi-Academy Trust in the South West of England that promotes the delivery of excellent educational experiences for our pupils, improving their life chances.
Welcome to our Federation
The Cabot Learning Federation is a family of 36 schools in Bristol, Gloucestershire, South Gloucestershire, North Somerset and Somerset. We are a mature multi-academy trust (MAT) serving communities in the South West. We lead the Five Counties Teaching School Hubs Alliance and School-Centred Initial Teacher Training (SCITT) and the Boolean Maths Hub, professional development provisions delivered from our CLF Institute.
​Instinctively collaborative and ambitious, our trust supports 18,000 children and young people aged 2 to 19 in a diverse array of settings and more than 3,000 employees. Whether you are a school or MAT wishing to join our family, an educator looking for a new opportunity or a parent or young person who simply wants to find out more about us, welcome and we look forward to hearing from you.

Curriculum overview
Our curriculum focuses upon acquiring key knowledge and builds upon what students have previously learned. The content of our curriculum is academically rigorous and seeks to remove barriers to create equity of opportunity for all young people. We are passionate about addressing the effects that experiencing disadvantage can have on young people so they can fulfil their true potential throughout life.
To help equip students to keep themselves safe in school, outside school and in the future, safeguarding is an integral part of our planned curriculum.​
In Key Stage 3 we intentionally provide a broad and balanced curriculum and in Key Stage 4 option subjects are offered based upon student need and our experience of where students are successful. We recognise the value of the EBacc and are working towards the government’s ambition.​
The curriculum is delivered by subject experts who are given the autonomy to adapt our curriculum to our context and consider the needs of the students in their classes. We emphasise the importance of improving pedagogy supported by research and national developments. Lessons are well planned and sequenced to ensure progression and that they are accessible to all.​ Adaptive teaching is an integral strand of our approach.
Reading is a key area of focus within Tewkesbury Academy. Our approach to reading falls within two strands – whole school reading and reading interventions. Our aim is to ensure that all students possess the reading skills needed to access the curriculum presented to them, as well as the opportunities open to them upon leaving the school.​
Our extra-curricular programme encourages our students to look for opportunities to lead and work as part of a team, with the programme designed to develop a wide range of qualities and skills. Students are offered a variety of activities including the Duke of Edinburgh award, highly-successful sports teams, popular performing arts opportunities and a range of weekly clubs.​
We encourage students to explore their future options and create opportunities for themselves by explicitly teaching careers. Our careers education programme starts in Year 7 and is embedded in every stage to ensure pupils are informed and prepared for an ever-changing workplace. At Key Stage 4, every student is offered independent careers advice from our level 6 trained Careers and Enterprise Coach.
Tewkesbury Academy is a place where staff are enthused and encourage a love of learning in students. We have strong outcomes, high expectations and a deep-rooted moral purpose. Our desire is for every student leaving Tewkesbury Academy to be equipped with the right qualifications, skills and qualities to empower them for a successful future.
For further information regarding our curriculum, please use the links below and visit our subject information pages, where you will find detailed curriculum overviews and knowledge organisers for each subject. If you have any further queries, please contact:info@ta.clf.uk and you will be directed to the appropriate Senior Leader.
